_comment: Cross-client price-input parsing (T-275). ONE file, read by BOTH test suites:
web/src/lib/priceParse.test.ts imports it, and Android's ItemFormViewModelTest reads it from
the repo root the way ExpenseMathTest reads expense-arithmetic.json.
Grammar: accept a comma decimal separator (normalized to a dot), strip all whitespace, then
strip AT MOST ONE currency symbol (€$£¥) from the START and AT MOST ONE from the END of what
remains. A symbol anywhere else in the string is left in place, so it fails the amount shape
and the whole input is rejected — never silently deleted ("1€5" must never become "15").
What is left must match [0-9]{1,13}(\.[0-9]{1,2})? (the digit cap is T-262's; see
expense-arithmetic.json's to_cents_invalid group for the crash that motivated it). A blank
input (after trimming) is valid with a null value, meaning 'no price'.
Android used to strip a currency symbol from ANYWHERE in the string (a character filter), so
"1€5" saved as 15.00 there and was correctly rejected on the web — this table pins the web's
ends-only grammar, now shared by both.
Each case gives 'valid' and, when valid, the normalized 'value' (null for a blank input).
An invalid case's exact message is locale text on the web and a string resource on Android, so
this table does not compare it — each suite's own tests already cover that.

amount.name: a comma decimal separator normalizes to a dot
whitespace and a trailing currency symbol are stripped
a leading currency symbol is stripped
a trailing currency symbol is stripped
one symbol at each end are both stripped
a leading symbol and a comma decimal both apply
an embedded symbol is left in place and rejected, never deleted (T-275)
a second leading symbol is not stripped (only one from each end)
a blank value has no price
an empty string has no price
trailing garbage after the digits is rejected
more than two decimal places is rejected
digits beyond the shared bound are rejected (T-262)
the amount that used to crash Android's toCents is rejected here too, up front
exactly at the digit bound is accepted (T-262)
non-ASCII digits are rejected, matching the server (T-125)
